negative_findings.description: No dedicated Ukrainian ATM / cash-handling / cash-in-transit industry association with a public member directory was located. negative_findings.result_summary: Ukrainian-language search returned bank associations and vendors, not a cash-handling association; the closest structural analogue found is APITU on the IT-equipment side, and EAST (European, via EMA's partner page) on the ATM-security side.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The ATM/cash-handling segment is central to hardware vendor and competitor mapping (Printec's own segment). Without an association pointer, that segment must be reached via NBU cash-circulation regulation, bank tender records, and EMA's EAST link instead.

brief: Ukraine's association layer is unusually generous for vendor and competitor discovery: EMA (ema.com.ua) publishes an open, link-rich member grid spanning Visa/Mastercard, ~35 banks, PSPs and hardware suppliers including Printec, plus a partner page that maps the whole institutional network and conference pages that expose tiered vendor sponsors. UAFIC complements it on the fintech/startup side, and its annual Ukrainian Fintech Catalog (257 companies in the 2025 edition, NBU- and IFC-backed) is effectively a downloadable actor census with a 2023 edition available for churn comparison. The bank demand side is triangulable across three overlapping rosters — NABU (>95% of system assets), AUB (70+ members, with an English mirror) and UKBS (~92 institutions) — while IT Ukraine and APITU cover the integrator and IT-equipment channels. The clear structural hole is ATM/cash-handling: no Ukrainian sector association for that segment was found in Ukrainian-language search, so that vendor set must be reached via NBU cash regulation, EAST via EMA, and tender records instead. All directories are Ukrainian-language-only in practice; NABU rate-limited on first contact and fintechua.org is client-rendered, so both need a more patient collector rather than being written off.
